We'll open a fresh V2-targeted PR once that implementation is ready.

Closing this approach because batching generic emitter dispatch changes listener semantics. `createGlobalEmitter` runs global listeners before typed listeners; Solid defers reactive propagation until the outer batch completes, so later typed listeners can observe stale projected state. The existing `restores queued compaction from durable pending input` test passes on the parent and deterministically times out here.

The installed `batchEmits` helper is not an alternative: it batches each emit independently and does not combine an event burst. Event scheduling needs a narrower projection boundary or removal of the current reducer/listener ordering dependency before this optimization is safe.

- Removed the configured `wsl:Ubuntu-26.04` entry from `opencode.settings`

> Any solutions that do not nuke the session DB? I want to continue my sessions. Any SQLite queries I could run?

There are multiple PRs open to fully fix the issue,  #37707 , #34188  and the closed one #31121. 

For session and message table you can follow manual migration:

- Move DB
``` 
mv ~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db ~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db.bak
```
- Open/close Opencode to create new DB.
- Connect to DB:
```sqlite3 ~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db ```
- Check the ID for the project in the old and the new DB (for me it changed):
``` SELECT id, worktree, name FROM project; ```
- Attach old DB:
``` ATTACH DATABASE '.local/share/opencode/opencode.db.bak' AS old; ```
- Import the sessions (replace project IDs):
```
INSERT INTO session (
  id, project_id, workspace_id, parent_id, slug, directory, path, title, version, share_url,
  summary_additions, summary_deletions, summary_files, summary_diffs, metadata,
  cost, tokens_input, tokens_output, tokens_reasoning, tokens_cache_read, tokens_cache_write,
  revert, permission, agent, model, time_created, time_updated, time_compacting, time_archived
)
SELECT
  s.id,
  '<NEW_PROJECT_ID>',
  NULL, s.parent_id, s.slug, s.directory, NULL, s.title, s.version, s.share_url,
  s.summary_additions, s.summary_deletions, s.summary_files, s.summary_diffs, NULL,
  0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0,
  s.revert, s.permission, NULL, NULL, s.time_created, s.time_updated, s.time_compacting, s.time_archived
FROM old.session s
WHERE s.project_id = '<OLD_PROJECT_ID>';
```
- Import messages (replace project ID):
```
INSERT INTO message
SELECT m.* FROM old.message m
WHERE m.session_id IN (
  SELECT id FROM old.session WHERE project_id = '<OLD_PROJECT_ID>'
);

INSERT INTO part
SELECT p.* FROM old.part p
WHERE p.session_id IN (
  SELECT id FROM old.session WHERE project_id = '<OLD_PROJECT_ID>'
);
```
- You should see sessions and messages restored
- If you need other tables you need to migrate them

I am not the PR's creator, but I request this PR be reopened. This PR is still an absolutely necessary resolution to a bug in OpenCode that causes tool calls to trigger an error and terminate agents. This PR is related to an open issue 30221 which still requires its resolution to be delivered.

OpenCode, as it is now, is completely unreliable to use because once this bug occurs, the running session is unrecoverable. Any further tool calls, in the same session, will trigger the same error and termination 100% of the time.

Automating the closing of such a valuable PR is completely unwise. You should not close PRs simply because the OpenCode team has yet to have time to review and approved/reject them, for existing an open bug.

> > Any interest in just rewriting the backend in Rust?
> 
> While rewriting it in Rust could address issues such as memory management and improve overall reliability, there are several practical considerations beyond the technical advantages.
> 
> The current project benefits not only from the efforts of its developers and open-source contributors, but also from regular updates, strong CI/CD pipelines, and the extensive code generation and maintenance assistance provided by ChatGPT 5 models through OpenRouter. In contrast, AI-assisted Rust development is still noticeably less capable than for languages like Python or TypeScript, based on my experience. Even wiring the entire system together in Rust is a substantial engineering effort.
> 
> More importantly, a rewrite would likely require several months of stabilization to identify and resolve regressions and newly introduced bugs. It is also unclear whether the project has a sufficiently active Rust contributor base or whether the core team possesses deep Rust expertise. Given that the project has evolved beyond a purely community-driven open-source initiative, long-term maintainability and contributor familiarity become equally important considerations alongside Rust's technical benefits.

Thanks for the consideration. I realize that asking project authors to entirely switch language is no small ask, and that of course ecosystem matters a lot.

I just want to share that, in my experience, AI-generated code works quite well with Rust. My impression is that the compiler and impeccable error reporting of Rust helps agents a lot. So far I've built 2 Rust projects this way across both closed and open weight models.

So, I was genuinely surprised to read: "AI-assisted Rust development is still noticeably less capable than for languages like Python or TypeScript, based on my experience", since my experience has been so significantly opposite of yours.

I genuinely love working with OpenCode, but the backend flakiness is definitely pushing me toward switching to some alternative. Right now, much of the troubles I'm seeing are probably more driven by the problems that Moonshot is having, since their Kimi K3 is continually returning 4XX codes, since their servers are under heavy stress right now (if you haven't heard, the company has shutoff new user signups while they try to scale to meet demand). I also see a lot of crashing / hanging with Z.ai GLM-5.2 (I don't know what their situation is).

My apologies if this is not the right place or form for such a report.

I can appreciate that it's a difficult task trying to support all these different providers and I imagine that it's a chaotic space to be working in. But I do feel that's all the more reason to employ a technology like Rust, since it will have your back much better than anything else, IMHO. I sincerely hope OpenCode is a long-term success. ✌️☮️

Upstream VTE bug report filed: https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/vte/-/work_items/2957

This is confirmed to be a VTE 0.76.0 bug triggered when two tabs in the same GNOME Terminal process both enter mouse tracking mode, corrupting X11 pointer grab state. Workaround: use separate terminal windows (Ctrl+Shift+N) instead of tabs for multiple opencode instances.
